parsed.notes: Reviewed all 7 group_inventory rows exactly once. No separate quote_fidelity, pincite, or black_letter rows were present in the inventory.

reasons: Lake identity gives case_name New York v. Class, court U.S. Supreme Court, date_decided 1986-02-25, and year 1986.
Lake citations give official cite 475 U.S. 106, vendor-neutral cite 1986 U.S. LEXIS 5, and the same three parallel cites listed in the page.
The opinion frames the question as a VIN inspection after the driver had been stopped for a traffic violation and exited the car.
The reasonableness holding expressly relies on the fact that officers observed Class commit two traffic violations.

defect.evidence_quote: We hold that this search was sufficiently unintrusive to be constitutionally permissible in light of the lack of a reasonable expectation of privacy in the VIN and the fact that the officers observed respondent commit two traffic violations.
defect.problem: The holding is directionally supported but too compressed: the reasonableness of reaching into the car depended on the specific traffic-stop circumstances, not merely on an obscured VIN.
defect.proposed_fix: There is no reasonable expectation of privacy in a VIN required by law to be visible; in the circumstances of a lawful traffic stop after officers observed two traffic violations and the driver had exited, a limited reach into the car to move papers obscuring the VIN was sufficiently unintrusive and reasonable.

reasons: The no-expectation-in-the-VIN portion is directly supported by the opinion.
The search portion survives only with the opinion's factual limits: observed traffic violations, an exited driver, an obscured VIN, and a limited reach to the VIN area.
residual_risks: Without the traffic-stop limitation, readers could overread Class as authorizing entry into a vehicle whenever a VIN is obscured.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add the traffic-stop and limited-intrusion conditions to the holding field.

reasons: The opinion repeatedly treats the VIN's mandated visibility from outside the automobile as central to the privacy analysis.
The role is only Related (cross-doctrine), which is supported by the opinion's plain-view/VIN reasoning.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep this no stronger than Related; Class is not a general plain-view seizure holding.

reasons: The opinion expressly holds that there was no reasonable expectation of privacy in the VIN.
The page's home role is cross-doctrine rather than claiming this is the lead reasonable-expectation case.
